$comment: Compliance control matrix: the rule, where it comes from, how this site satisfies it, and the automated check that makes 'we satisfy it' a build result rather than an assertion. Gate ids map to functions in scripts/checks.mjs.
reviewed_against: Amazon Associates Program Operating Agreement (fetched 2026-11-20, page dated 2025-10-15)
Amazon Associates Program Policies (linked, body not fetched - see S02)
FTC Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking (S03, S04)

controls.rule: State the participation sentence, clear and prominent, on the Site.
controls.implementation: Disclosure strip rendered under the masthead on every page, plus the same sentence in the footer of every page, plus the /disclosure/ page as the long form.
controls.gate: every HTML file in docs/ must contain the exact sentence; a page without it fails the build

controls.rule: Do not bury or hyperlink away the disclosure.
controls.origin: FTC: a button labelled DISCLOSURE that links to a full disclosure is not clear and conspicuous (S04)
controls.implementation: The strip is inline text, always visible above the fold, never a tooltip, never below a 'read more'. The /disclosure/ page supplements it and is linked from it, which is permitted as well as the text.
controls.gate: the disclosure sentence must appear in the first 2,000 characters of the body, not only inside a link or a footer

controls.rule: Disclose the material connection in unambiguous words near the endorsement.
controls.implementation: Every sponsored anchor carries a 'Sponsored' chip and a link-level line in plain words. No '#ad' style shorthand is used on the site itself, since the audience is readers not followers.
controls.gate: each a[data-aff] must sit within an element carrying a disclosure class, and must be preceded by a labelled sponsor chip

controls.rule: Links must use the special 'tagged' link formats provided by Amazon.
controls.implementation: All commerce anchors are generated by scripts/build.mjs in the form https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=<tracking-id>&linkCode=ll1&language=en_US. No hand-written link can reach the output.
controls.gate: every amazon.com anchor must carry tag= matching register/site.json tracking_id; a mismatch or missing tag fails the build
controls.status: passing with caveat - the tracking ID's existence on the account is unverified (S09). Format passes; enrolment is a human step.

controls.rule: Do not imply Amazon support, sponsorship or endorsement.
controls.implementation: No 'recommended by', no Amazon logo, no 'official' framing, and no use of Amazon's name beyond the required sentence and factual references to the listings. The methodology page states the relationship in flat terms.
controls.gate: banned-phrase list in register/site.json voice.banned_words is matched case-insensitively across all content

controls.rule: Do not publish Program Content images outside the licensed path.
controls.origin: Operating Agreement s.1 (Program Content definition) and the IP licence it incorporates
controls.implementation: Original generated art only, captioned as illustration. No m.media-amazon.com asset is referenced anywhere in the tree.
controls.gate: build fails if any output HTML references an Amazon CDN host

controls.rule: Price and availability may only appear when Amazon supplies the data; cached data must be refreshed within 24 hours.
controls.origin: Program Policies as described by secondary sources (S02) - wording unresolved, so the site takes the strict path
controls.implementation: No price, no availability, no star rating, no review count, anywhere. Product pages carry a 'what we did not verify' panel that explains the blank instead of filling it.
controls.gate: regular expression over docs/ for a currency pattern ([$]\d) and for star-rating phrasing; any hit fails the build

controls.rule: Mark paid/affiliate outbound links so search engines understand why they exist.
controls.origin: Google Search Central, qualify outbound links (S10)
controls.implementation: rel="sponsored nofollow" on every commerce anchor, plus noopener noreferrer for the target=_blank pair.
controls.gate: each amazon.com anchor's rel attribute must contain both sponsored and nofollow

controls.rule: Do not make claims the evidence does not support.
controls.origin: FTC Act s.5 deception principle as applied to endorsements (S03); project's own no-hallucination instruction
controls.implementation: No search-volume, popularity, trend or superiority claim appears. The brief's suggested titles are used as topics, phrased as questions. Every numeric statement is either an official citation or an observation with a source row.
controls.gate: claims register: any sentence in content/ containing a number must resolve to a source_id, else the build warns and the reviewer must accept it

controls.rule: Handle reader data lawfully and minimally.
controls.origin: Project decision, informed by the absence of any consent layer on a static host
controls.implementation: No cookies, no localStorage identity, no third-party scripts, no email capture (SG-30 explains why the slot is empty). Privacy page states exactly what is and is not collected.
controls.gate: no Set-Cookie, no external script src, and no known tracker host in any output file

controls.rule: Keep the intended identifier and the observed redirect target as separate fields.
controls.implementation: register/products.json has intended_asin (null, unknown) and observed_redirect_target (populated). Nothing merges them, and no page calls the observed ASIN 'the product you chose'.
controls.gate: schema check in scripts/checks.mjs asserts the two fields exist separately on every row

controls.rule: Register each Site where Program Content appears.
controls.origin: Participation Requirements (referenced by s.12 of the Agreement; page not fetched)
controls.implementation: Not done and cannot be done from here. It is the top line of the owner-action list and blocks monetisation, not publication.
controls.gate: none available - manual step, surfaced on /decisions/ as Q-07

gate_summary.principle: Anything a machine can verify runs on every build and blocks the merge. Anything it cannot is put in front of a human with the exact screen to open - never quietly assumed.
